items.title: Jack DeJohnette — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: I was going to have him play on this piece, but he passed away in that week.

ctx.x: So this must have been a very extended project. You’re talking about rehearsals…

It was quite a project and then comes the subject of Miles. Miles had actually passed away in that period . . . and I immediately wrote this piece for Miles called “Miles,” which featured two drums. Two drums can really work good when they’re working in synch, especially to groove. James Brown did it. B.B. King uses two drummers. Will and I really locked together. The groove was killer so we did that, and then I wrote something called “Darkness To Light.” This was my electric writing. Another loss of that period…
